author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Dick's unpublished theological notes behind A Maze of Death, filed in the archive as "Notes on the Tench Novel," working out the novel's invented religion of Mentufacturer, Intercessor, and Walker-on-Earth.
page_summary:
This sixteen-page unpublished document, titled "Notes on the Tench Novel" in the archive itself, contains the theological and conceptual groundwork behind A Maze of Death (1970). Dick built that novel around a fully invented religion, and these notes show him constructing its doctrine, chiefly the tripartite deity of the Mentufacturer, the Intercessor, and the Walker-on-Earth, a homemade theology that both structures the novel's world and is eventually revealed within it as a coping mechanism aboard a doomed spacecraft.

The notes are unusually revealing about Dick's method, catching him at the point where speculative theology and narrative machinery are still fused. The same questions that animate the novel, whether a manufactured god can be real, whether prayer can be answered by a system that the characters themselves designed, are here worked out as premises rather than dramatized as plot.

The portal holds one archive manifestation, dated circa 1968. It connects directly to the portal's Exegesis work-record for A Maze of Death and anticipates the theological problems Dick would pursue for the rest of his life.
